tracks.narration: How do you copy a current from one branch of a chip to another, without measuring it?
Two matched NPN transistors share their bases and emitters. Q one is diode connected — its collector ties back to its base — and a reference resistor sets the current that flows through it.
Both transistors see the same V B E. Because collector current depends only on V B E, the two collector currents are equal — Q two simply copies the current set by R reference.
Change R reference and I reference moves. I out tracks it in lockstep — that's the mirror in action.
Current mirrors are the workhorse bias circuit inside almost every analog integrated chip — op-amps, references, amplifiers.
